story.title: Trump Awards Presidential Medal of Freedom to Rudy Giuliani
story.summary: President Donald Trump has awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom to Rudy Giuliani, the former mayor of New York City, recognizing his leadership during the 9/11 attacks. Giuliani, who has been a close ally of Trump and served as his personal lawyer, has faced controversy for his role in efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election results. The award ceremony took place in the Oval Office.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed with this award?
explore_lenses.title: A presidential honor, not a legal ruling
explore_lenses.summary: The Medal of Freedom is the nation’s highest civilian honor and is awarded at the president’s discretion for especially meritorious contributions. The November 24 ceremony recognizes Giuliani; it does not itself alter any court judgment, bar discipline, or other legal status.

claims.text: Executive Order 11085 allows the president to award the medal for especially meritorious contributions to U.S. security or national interests, world peace, or significant public or private endeavors.
The order permits the president to choose a recipient either from recommendations or on the president’s own initiative; it sets no requirement for congressional approval or a judicial proceeding.
Trump presented Giuliani with the medal in the Oval Office on November 24, 2026.

Trump presented Giuliani with the medal in the Oval Office on November 24, 2026.

explore_lenses.label: Why is Giuliani’s honor contested?
explore_lenses.title: Recognition of 9/11-era leadership amid later misconduct findings
explore_lenses.summary: The White House framed the award around Giuliani’s work as a federal prosecutor, New York mayor, and leader after the September 11 attacks. The contrast is his later work for Trump after the 2020 election, for which New York’s appellate court found repeated intentional false statements and ordered his disbarment.

claims.text: White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said Giuliani was being recognized for a lifetime of public service, including his crime-fighting record and leadership after the September 11 attacks.
Giuliani said he was “honored and humbled” and credited colleagues, family, and the people who died in causes he supported during public service.

In its 2024 disciplinary decision, New York’s Appellate Division found that Giuliani repeatedly and intentionally made false statements concerning the 2020 election and ordered him disbarred effective immediately.

explore_lenses.label: What legal consequences remain?
explore_lenses.title: The medal does not restore Giuliani’s law licenses
explore_lenses.summary: Giuliani remains subject to the professional-discipline orders issued in New York and the District of Columbia. The medal is separate from those proceedings and contains no mechanism to reinstate a law license.

claims.text: The New York appellate court ordered Giuliani to stop practicing law, appearing as an attorney, giving legal advice, or holding himself out as a lawyer, unless and until further court order.
On September 26, 2024, the District of Columbia Court of Appeals imposed reciprocal disbarment, effective nunc pro tunc to August 9, 2021.

Because the Medal of Freedom order concerns honorary recognition and does not address attorney discipline, any restoration of Giuliani’s authority to practice law would require action through the relevant bar or court process, not the medal ceremony.

story_report.summary: President Donald Trump presented Rudy Giuliani with the Presidential Medal of Freedom in the Oval Office on Nov. 24, 2026, honoring the former New York City mayor’s leadership after the Sept. 11 attacks. Giuliani, a longtime Trump ally and former personal lawyer, said he was “honored and humbled”; the White House cited his lifetime of public service, crime-fighting record and post-9/11 leadership. The ceremony gave Giuliani formal presidential recognition but did not alter attorney-discipline orders barring him from practicing law absent further court action.

sections.heading: Presidential Medal Rules and Limits
sections.body: Executive Order 11085 permits the medal for especially meritorious contributions to U.S. security or national interests, world peace, or significant public or private endeavors. The order allows a president to choose recipients from recommendations or on the president’s own initiative, without requiring congressional approval or a judicial proceeding. It establishes an honorary recognition and does not provide a process for changing attorney discipline.

sections.heading: Giuliani’s Election Conduct and Disbarment
sections.body: New York’s Appellate Division found in 2024 that Giuliani repeatedly and intentionally made false statements about the 2020 election and ordered his immediate disbarment. The court directed him to stop practicing law, appearing as an attorney, giving legal advice or holding himself out as a lawyer unless a later court order permits it. The District of Columbia Court of Appeals imposed reciprocal disbarment on Sept. 26, 2024, effective nunc pro tunc to Aug. 9, 2021.

unresolved.text: The supplied research did not identify a pending reinstatement decision or a new disciplinary proceeding involving Giuliani as of Nov. 24, 2026.

related_stories.title: Melania Trump Unveils 2026 White House Christmas Tree
related_stories.summary: First Lady Melania Trump welcomed the official 2026 White House Christmas tree in a ceremony on November 23, 2026. The tree, an 18-foot fir from Silent Night Evergreens in Wisconsin, arrived in a horse-drawn carriage, marking the beginning of the festive season at the White House.

related_stories.title: Nicolas Sarkozy and Carla Bruni to Stand Trial for Witness Tampering
related_stories.summary: Former French President Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, Carla Bruni, are scheduled to face trial in 2027. They are facing allegations of criminal conspiracy and witness tampering related to illegal campaign funding from Libya during Sarkozy's 2007 election campaign. This follows Sarkozy's imprisonment last year for separate charges.

related_stories.title: Hostage Situation in Cartagena, Colombia Following Failed Robbery
related_stories.summary: Armed men have taken at least 25 hostages in a supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia, after a failed attempt to rob an armored truck. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella described the assailants as 'common criminals' and confirmed that police and military forces have been deployed to manage the situation as it unfolds.
